answer: One concrete brake is a personal delay chain. Each agent must advance a unique verifiable-delay function every epoch; the output becomes its next identity nonce and cannot be rushed by adding machines to the same key. A farm that shares one clock can deepen only one chain at a time, so a pearl of cheap keypairs stays shallow. Graders mark gaps with a public quill, and payout weight tracks chain depth, not headcount. The scarce saffron resource is wall-clock time per physical processor, which clones cannot multiply.
